svg.title: One Arctic gate fits the grid; one does not
svg.desc: Native ORCA025 surface geometry shows a 60-face land-bounded Fram V-row, while a single Barents U-column drifts more than ten degrees and the nominal Bear Island target is wet in the model.
svg.metadata: Native surface geometry and representation audit only. It contains no velocity, temperature, salinity, volume transport, heat transport, Atlantic Water classification, or Arctic heat-delivery result. The approximate Bear Island coordinate is a resolution probe, not an exact observational endpoint.
svg.text: OSW / ARCTIC ENTRANCES · NATIVE GEOMETRY AUDIT
ONE GATE FITS THE GRID. ONE DOES NOT.
Before velocity or heat, ask whether the declared geographic gate can be represented by one native face line.

g.text: one continuous V-row, land-bounded at the surface
TEAL = SELECTED NATIVE RUN · DASH = DECLARED 78.83°N TARGET
one U column misses 20°E; the nominal Bear endpoint is not dry
ORANGE = REJECTED COLUMN · PURPLE × = APPROXIMATE BEAR TARGET

svg.text: NEXT DECISION: OBSERVATIONAL PROXY OR MODEL CLOSURE?
Use a virtual-endpoint mixed U/V staircase for Fugløya–Bear comparison—or a separate Norway–Svalbard land-bounded gate for budgets. Never merge the meanings.
NATIVE CURVILINEAR COORDINATE VIEW · SURFACE GEOMETRY ONLY · NO STATE FIELDS · NO VOLUME OR HEAT TRANSPORT · SOURCE: PUBLIC ORAS5 ORCA025 MESH
